page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc7.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical Intel Xeon 8369HB cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a base clock speed of 3.3 GHz, the processor includes a 33 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX-512_VNNI, and AVX-512_BF16. The instance is equipped with 96.0 GB of RAM, providing a compute-focused allocation of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, and operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark results position this instance in the average tier for most compute and memory tasks, with some notable strengths. It achieves a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 206.84 GB/sec and a Passmark memory score of 2865.83, both placing in the top 25% of tested hardware. Standard multi-core performance is solid, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 49887.09 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12926.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 113.29 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 51.8 GB/sec for writes. For database and web serving workloads, it delivers 40.04 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 27.12 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The instance offers a high-density compute profile, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. The lack of bundled local SSDs means users must rely on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for I/O-heavy operations. Additionally, the absence of a GPU limits its utility for large-scale deep learning, though it handles small to medium LLM inference reasonably well, processing 68.85 tokens/sec for 7B model prompts. This server is best suited for high-performance computing, multi-threaded compilation, web serving, and medium-scale database operations.
